A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monazite and zircon are stable during the melting of tonalitic and metapelitic protoliths, but that the growth of allanite is favoured during the melting of granodioritic and metapeliti protoliths.

the monazite U-Pb system is a useful dating tool for partially melted rocks, but that its reliability is limited by its sensitivity to water activity during melting, and by the presence of older cores in the monazite grains.
the monazite and/or allanite U/Pb systematics are only useful for dating of partial melting if the monazite is not affected by the growth of younger allanite and/or if allanite is absent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monazite is stable during the entire melting process, even in the presence of high Ca concentrations and high water activities.
monazite is stable in all the studied anatexite types.
